017package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.AssertionUtils.*;
020
021import java.util.concurrent.atomic.*;
022
023import org.apache.juneau.bean.jsonrpc.*;
024import org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.*;
025
026/**
027 * Dispatches server-initiated JSON-RPC requests delivered over an MCP client's duplex event-stream channel to a
028 * single registered {@link McpServerRequestHandler}.
029 *
030 * <p>
031 * Requests are handed to the registered handler untouched, with their {@code params} left as the generic,
032 * revision-neutral wire representation - never projected into a typed request bean - since the set of
033 * server-initiated methods (for example {@code sampling/createMessage}; illustrative only, as sampling is
034 * deprecated per SEP-2577) is revision- and deployment-specific and this dispatcher has no knowledge of it.
035 *
036 * @since 10.0.0
037 */
038public class McpDuplexDispatcher {
039
040   // Argument name constants for assertArgNotNull
041   private static final String ARG_REQUEST = "request";
042
043   private final AtomicReference<McpServerRequestHandler> handler = new AtomicReference<>();
044
045   /**
046    * Registers (or de-registers) the handler invoked by {@link #dispatch(JsonRpcRequest, BeanStore)}.
047    *
048    * @param value The handler to register. Passing <jk>null</jk> de-registers any previously-registered handler -
049    *    a subsequent {@link #dispatch(JsonRpcRequest, BeanStore)} call then behaves as if no handler was ever
050    *    registered (see the "no handler" behavior documented there).
051    * @return This object.
052    */
053   public McpDuplexDispatcher register(McpServerRequestHandler value) {
054      handler.set(value);
055      return this;
056   }
057
058   /**
059    * Dispatches a single server-initiated request to the registered handler.
060    *
061    * <p>
062    * When no handler is registered: a notification (a <jk>null</jk> {@link JsonRpcRequest#getId() id}) is
063    * silently dropped (returns <jk>null</jk>); a request is rejected with a {@code -32601} {@link McpException}.
064    *
065    * @param request The inbound request. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
066    * @param ctx The request-scoped bean store to hand to the handler. Can be <jk>null</jk>, in which case
067    *    {@link BasicBeanStore#INSTANCE} is used instead.
068    * @return The handler's result, or <jk>null</jk> for a notification with no registered handler.
069    * @throws McpException If no handler is registered and {@code request} is not a notification, or if the
070    *    handler itself throws (an {@link McpException} thrown by the handler propagates as-is; any other
071    *    exception is wrapped as a {@code -32603} internal-error {@link McpException} with the original
072    *    exception preserved as its cause).
073    */
074   public Object dispatch(JsonRpcRequest request, BeanStore ctx) {
075      assertArgNotNull(ARG_REQUEST, request);
076      var h = handler.get();
077      if (h == null) {
078         if (JsonRpcResponse.notification(request.getId()))
079            return null;
080         throw new McpException(-32601, String.format("No server-request handler registered for method '%s'", request.getMethod()));
081      }
082      try {
083         return h.handle(request, ctx == null ? BasicBeanStore.INSTANCE : ctx);
084      } catch (McpException e) {
085         throw e;
086      } catch (Exception e) {
087         var e2 = new McpException(-32603, "Internal error handling server request '" + request.getMethod() + "'");
088         e2.initCause(e);
089         throw e2;
090      }
091   }
092}
